channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [EU Observer] What kind of ECB is Europe getting after Lagarde?
item.description: Now that Paris and Berlin appear to have lined up Spanish central banker Pablo Hernández de Cos for the ECB presidency instead of his Dutch counterpart Klaas Knot, whether a dove or a hawk sits at the top may matter less than it seems, including for France.

item.title: [EU Observer] Xi keen to look ‘neutral’ on Ukraine at Shenzhen summit, as China risks spoiling EU relations by helping Putin to wage war
item.description: As Xi, Putin, and Trump gather in Shenzhen, Beijing is stretching its “neutral” pose to maintain a war‑fuelling trade lifeline for Moscow.

item.title: [EU Observer] Centrist and leftwing MEPs boycott rightwing NGO funding probe, which found no wrongdoing
item.description: As rightwing MEPs present their 71-page NGO funding report, centre and left-wing deputies stay away in protest, accusing the scrutiny group of bending parliament rules and sidelining their input.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU auditors say rules ‘full of holes’ leave health at risk from toxic forever chemicals
item.description: Three eggs or a beef steak contain a dangerous amount of cancerous forever chemicals and yet it can take up to a decade before new harmful substances are banned under EU law.

item.title: [EU Observer] Bridge Wars: Putin’s iconic Crimean Bridge destroyed despite ‘elite’ air-defences, but vital Kyiv bridge also close to collapse (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,728)
item.description: The sudden collapse of the Crimean Bridge’s key span, combined with precision Russian strikes on Kyiv’s lifeline bridges, threaten to choke off entire cities on both sides.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU opts for voluntary targets to secure key materials used in high-tech industries
item.description: The blueprint announced on Wednesday is the latest move by the EU executive to make the bloc's industrial base more self-reliant, but lacks a legal base.

item.title: [EU Observer] Hungary digs up €17m in buried cash during probe into Orbán-era minister Seszták
item.description: Miklós Seszták, a minister under Viktor Orbán, is under investigation by Péter Magyar’s new anti-corruption body — and it took 12 treasury staff, five banknote-counting machines and eight hours to tally the €17m in buried cash linked to him.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU Commission ‘confident’ that Bulgaria, Czech Republic, Hungary, and Slovakia will join new €45bn Ukraine loan
item.description: The EU Commission has come up with a new financing plan to fill Ukraine's €70bn funding gap next year, and thinks it has found a way to convince member states who want to opt-out by clearly separating civilian from military spending

item.title: [DW] Hashim Thaci's second conviction in The Hague reignites debate in Kosovo about justice and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers
item.description: Former President Hashim Thaci has been convicted of trying to influence witnesses in his war crimes trial. The conviction has reignited debate in Kosovo about the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, the court that convicted him.

item.title: [DW] Back to 1997: Russia wants NATO to roll back its eastern expansion
item.description: The Kremlin is reportedly calling on NATO to withdraw from large parts of Eastern Europe. What this would mean for the security of millions of Europeans — and what lies behind Russia's plan.

item.title: [DW] Rights court rules Turkey must release jailed lawmaker Atalay
item.description: The European Court of Human Rights has called for the release of imprisoned elected lawmaker Can Atalay. Atalay has been in prison for almost five years despite rulings from the Turkish Constitutional Court.

item.title: [DW] Students' List candidates take seats as Serbian parliament opens
item.description: Serbia's Student List's candidates have taken their oaths in the inaugural parliament session. As the new majority, they have 90 days to form a government.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Zucman, le retour
item.description: Un manifeste publié ce vendredi, un “sommet contre l’oligarchie internationale” samedi, une proposition de taxe supplémentaire : Gabriel Zucman est de retour au premier plan. Engagé dans une démarche de plus en plus politique, l’économiste français de 40 ans veut peser sur le débat de la présidentielle. Comment compte-t-il s’y prendre ? Pèse-t-il sur les […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] Trump presses European leaders about Ukraine aid in call after Putin summit
item.description: In a surprise call, the U.S. president followed up his meeting with Russian and Chinese leaders by quizzing Kyiv's European allies.

item.title: [Financial Times] Houthi air strike hits Saudi sovereign wealth fund headquarters
item.description: Attack on powerful Public Investment Fund follows near-daily barrages on the kingdom by Houthi rebels

item.title: [Financial Times] Anthropic shares indicated to open 33% higher at $110
item.description: AI giant to begin trading after raising $81bn in record IPO

item.title: [Politico Europe] Britain shouldn’t rush to a second Brexit referendum, say pro-EU Lib Dems
item.description: Al Pinkerton, the party's Europe spokesperson, says the public would have “an expectation” there would be a referendum on rejoining the bloc.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ukrainians hit Crimea’s railway bridge with Neptune missiles, but it is harder to destroy than the road bridge (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,729)
item.description: Ukraine’s strikes on the Crimean railway bridge and Russia’s refineries are no longer just symbolic blows, but a coordinated effort to choke off fuel, supplies, and troop movements deep inside Russian-held territory.

item.title: [Euractiv] China, US, Russia issue ‘Declaration toward Peace’ after first summit
item.description: Critics warned that the optics from the meeting would be damaging for the US president

item.title: [Financial Times] Putin invites European leaders to Moscow
item.description: Russian leader signals Russia is unwilling to relax hardline demands for ending Ukraine conflict

item.title: [EU Observer] EU gives oil and gas importers until 2029 on methane checks, rules out more delay
item.description: After all-night talks, EU governments and MEPs agreed to delay methane regulations until 2029, but scrapped the legal possibility for further fob-offs, in a win for centre-left politics.

item.title: [Euractiv] Lithuania vows to shield defence spending if MFF talks drag into 2027
item.description: Defence and space spending will be as 'untouchable' as CAP and cohesion, Kubilius says

item.title: [Euractiv] Drugs not the main driver of Ireland’s €1bn health overrun, says Labour deputy [Partner Content]
item.description: Ireland’s health minister says medicines account for 12% of the HSE deficit, and their cost will keep rising, but insists pay is where control must be shown

item.title: [DW] EU Commission confirms it was targeted in cyberattack using AI tools
item.description: The European Commission was targeted by an "AI-generated cybercampaign," a spokesperson has said. This is the first time the bloc has publicly reported an AI-based cyberattack.

item.title: [Financial Times] Gulf flare-up stokes fears of return to Iran war
item.description: A week of tit-for-tat escalation by Iran and the US has brought the countries closer to another full-scale confrontation, analysts say

item.title: [Euractiv] Unfunded cancer plans are unlikely to change care, All.Can president warns [Partner Content]
item.description: Governments do not need to fund a whole cancer plan at once, but they must make a start and plan a staged approach, says All.Can president Prof. Christobel Saunders

item.title: [Euractiv] No way forward on tapping Russian assets, Euroclear insists
item.description: Russia could retaliate against Euroclear by pursuing claims for damages

item.title: [Euractiv] COP31: Draft deal drops call to end fossil fuel use
item.description: References to a global electrification target remain as Australia seeks global consensus

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs gut EU Commission plan for regulating space industries
item.description: Brussels is racing to keep up in the global space race, after MEPs slashed green demands from the EU’s first Space Act, in a bid to win over capitals and industry.

item.title: [DW] Wadephul: 'Coalition of the Willing' talks in Berlin send strong signal to Moscow
item.description: German Foreign Minister Wadephul has said the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin sends a clear message to Moscow to take peace talks seriously. He also warned Ukraine should be prepared for peace talks to fail.

item.title: [Financial Times] The key to Anthropic’s value
item.description: The AI company needs to become a full enterprise technology platform after IPO

item.title: [Euractiv] EXCLUSIVE: France, Spain push for ‘big four’ telco asks in satellite-to-phone law
item.description: Europe's largest mobile operators worry about competing with US giant SpaceX

item.title: [Euractiv] Serbia elects academic as parliament speaker
item.description: Among his first tasks will be calling a snap presidential election

item.title: [Financial Times] Xi, Trump and Putin hail ‘groundbreaking’ meeting
item.description: The world’s three largest nuclear powers agree to talks on preventing proliferation

item.title: [Politico Europe] Startups call on Commission to salvage or scrap EU Inc proposal
item.description: Lobby groups call on Brussels to withdraw and resubmit after proposal for new corporate form was watered down by EU member countries.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Video: EU-Gesundheitskommissar wird aus Protest gegen Pestizidregeln mit „Asche“ beworfen
item.description: Olivér Várhelyi wollte gerade auf einem Krebsgipfel das Wort ergreifen, als eine graue Substanz auf ihn geworfen wurde.

item.title: [Euractiv] Activists throw ashes at EU health commissioner during speech
item.description: Protesters disrupt European Cancer Summit in Brussels over proposed EU pesticide changes

item.title: [Politico Europe] Nigel Farage is back in Brussels
item.description: The veteran Brexiteer is in town to attack Andy Burnham's efforts at building bridges with the EU.

item.title: [EU Observer] Erdoğan is strangling Turkey’s last free media, as EU turns a blind eye
item.description: Turkey's state takeover of independent broadcaster Sözcü TV was met by loud EU silence, in a broader pattern of appeasement, as Erdoğan strangles what is left of free speech.

item.title: [Euractiv] European Commission confirms AI-boosted cyberattack
item.description: A spokesperson on Thursday could not say whether the attacks were over

item.title: [Politico Europe] Présidentielle : pourquoi les youtubeurs ne veulent pas être régulés comme les télés
item.description: Dans un entretien à POLITICO, l’Umicc défend fermement ses positions face aux règles de pluralisme que veut soumettre l'Arcom aux créateurs de contenus.

item.title: [Euractiv] EU takes action against four countries over deforestation rules
item.description: Brussels gives the four countries two months to address shortcomings

item.title: [Financial Times] Ukraine’s western allies meet in Berlin to counter Yalta 2.0 optics
item.description: Germany hosts 40 delegations in show of solidarity for Kyiv while leaders of Russia, China and US meet in Shenzhen

item.title: [Politico Europe] Watch: EU health chief has ‘ashes’ thrown over him in protest at pesticide rules
item.description: Olivér Várhelyi was about to speak at a cancer summit when he had a grey substance thrown at him.

item.title: [Financial Times] Anthropic is a ‘must own’
item.description: Is that good?

item.title: [Euractiv] COP31: EU just ‘buying time’ with methane rules delay, Hoekstra says
item.description: Europe 'not wavering at all', EU climate commissioner insists while critics accuse Brussels of caving in

item.title: [Euractiv] Shenzhen: Trump says ‘making history’ with Putin and Xi
item.description: Berlin summit of Ukraine allies will try to act as counterweight to the big three

item.title: [Politico Europe] Spanish election race tightens ahead of campaign’s final week, new poll shows
item.description: The conservative People's Party and Socialists are neck and neck, with the far-right Vox in position to play kingmaker.

item.title: [Politico Europe] UK Tory chief Badenoch blasts ‘disturbing’ Trump-Putin-Xi trilateral
item.description: Right-wing Kemi Badenoch says Britain must now look beyond a U.S. 'administration on its way out.'

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Is the EU’s Digital Services Act actually working?
item.description: Earlier this week, the European Commission stepped up its action against Chinese online marketplace Temu. It announced that the platform was once again in breach of the Digital Services Act (DSA), and could face further fines.

item.title: [EU Observer] The same EU Parliament that built the Ethics Body is now killing it, in violation of European law
item.description: Two and a half years after signing the agreement, the EU Parliament is blocking its own ethics body before it has met even once, but EU law does not allow it to walk away so easily, and nor should parliament president Metsola.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU should tax Big Tech and crypto to help farmers in next budget, Spanish socialist MEP says
item.description: As EU leaders wrangle over Europe’s next long-term budget, socialist MEP Sandra Gómez López warns that unless Big Tech, online gambling, and crypto start paying more, farmers and poorer regions will be the ones footing the bill.

item.title: [Euractiv] FIREPOWER: NATO’s next-gen comms plan released
item.description: In today's edition: Coalition of the Willing, autonomous weapons, EU–UK

item.title: [Euractiv] THE HACK: Further privacy rule cuts not ruled out
item.description: In today's edition: MSS delays, OVHcloud, Space Act

item.title: [Financial Times] Angry America and its housing market
item.description: The country is failing to provide enough houses to enable people to move to where the good jobs are

item.title: [Financial Times] Gold loses its lustre for investors
item.description: Precious metal long touted as a diversifier for portfolios has not offered protection during recent tech stock fall

item.title: [Financial Times] Adani: the billionaire at the heart of Modi’s India
item.description: Three years ago, the tycoon was fending off lawsuits and accusations of fraud. Now, his business empire looks more powerful than ever

item.title: [Financial Times] Musk says he feels ‘foolish’ for donating nearly $500mn to Republicans
item.description: SpaceX CEO backs away from Maga after monetary support for Trump’s party in midterm elections fails to sway voters

item.title: [DW] EU leaders tussle over whom to send to Ukraine, Russia peace talks
item.description: A seat at the table for Europe now appears likely following comments by a US envoy who just held talks with Putin. But who will take that seat remains unclear.

item.title: [DW] Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?
item.description: The EU wants to curb subscription traps, misleading sales tactics and features that keep people scrolling. What would the proposed Digital Fairness Act change, and does it go far enough?

item.title: [DW] What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?
item.description: The first trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in nine months have ended with an agreement on exchanging prisoners. Does this mark a genuine breakthrough and a step toward peace?

item.title: [DW] Despite restrictive abortion laws, Poland's 'Abortomat' — a locker that dispenses abortion pills — helps women who want to end a pregnancy
item.description: Abortion laws in Poland are very restrictive. Activists there have found a new way to help women wanting to terminate a pregnancy: the "Abortomat," a locker that dispenses abortion pills. But they face fierce opposition.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine: Zelenskyy says security deal could go to referendum
item.description: The US has broached the idea of Kyiv giving up the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, the Ukrainian president said.

item.title: [DW] Turkey uses espionage accusations to pressure government critics
item.description: The arrest of a German foundation's employee in Istanbul this week has put the focus back on pressure tactics used by the Erdogan administration. The arrest is far from the first of its kind.

item.title: [DW] Gen Z protests: Do Baby Boomers really have it better than young people?
item.description: Should young people in Germany be more worried about their future than Baby Boomers were in the 1980s and 1990s? Or should both generations take to the streets and protest together? DW checked the data.

item.title: [DW] The dangers of revising Europe's security architecture
item.description: Experts warn against revising Europe's security framework because they say it would mean granting Moscow its longstanding wish of renegotiating postwar security on the continent.

item.title: [DW] Czechia braces for massive protest against public media reform plans
item.description: A fast-tracked bill to cut public media funding has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia. A massive protest is planned for Prague on Sunday.
